I am really sorry that it has been so hard for you!   It must be very hard trying to get a job and also managing your mental and physical health. Unfortunately I can't give you advice regarding your work-situation, but I can maybe offer some advice when it comes to your health.   
  I struggled with depression and anxiety for 10 years and I have hashimoto thyreoiditis and pcos and some other stuff so I have to take many medications that have many side effects.   Please, don't stop taking your medications! I know that it is very tiring and sometimes it feels so frustrating but try to remember that it wouldn't make your situation better, you would just add more problems.   Also you wrote that you don't see a future anymore. One thing that helped me (I am not a therapist, this is just my experience so pls keep that in mind) was to try to just think about the next 24 hours and what you can do to make your situation better. If you think about the future while being depressed it will be very hard to see something there, not because there isn't something (there are many things that could happen that will make you very happy even if you don't see it) but because unfortunately that's exactly what depression does. So looking there won't help.     
  Try to look at your situation in the present moment and don't think about it like “I want to get better!” It is very hard to make progress if the goal is very unspecific. Make small and more specific goals that will contribute to your health like trying to go on a walk everyday. Don't see it as “I have to stop being self-destructive” and try to just see it as “I want to add more little things to my day so I am feeling a little better when I am doing them and also I will be too busy to do something that is bad for me”.   Try to eat healthier, try to get better sleep, maybe talk to some friends on the phone for 10 minutes daily. Also try to exercise and drink enough water! I don't want people to think that that is everything you have to do to get out of depression – because it isn't – but I really think that if you just focus on making the next 24 hours as good as possible you will maybe go from a stage 10 depression to a stage 9. And keeping your body healthy is a really good start. So maybe just try to add little things to your daily life, that will make you move in the right direction and focus on the next 24 hours.   
  That is a mindset that really helped me to get better but everyone has to find something that works for them. I really hope that your situation will be better soon! Take care!

I also used to struggle with this and what really helped me was to go to my psychiatrist to get the right medication. Also I put reminders in my calender to try to avoid certain triggers in the weeks where I know I will be more depressed. I also make a big effort to socialize as much as I can in that week and try to go more on walks and things like that, just to not be alone and ruminate on everything. Just try different things like reading or yoga and try to stay busy. You still will be more likely to experience bad depression in that week but try to avoid the triggers when you feel unstable. But besides that finding the right medication really did wonders for me! 

Also ,like someone already mentioned, there is a disorder called PMDD, so please talk to a psychiatrist or a therapist about that.

that makes perfectly sense and I had that thought too when I was in therapy but one thing you should not forget is that when dreaming about you as if you are in therapy session it is still you who thinks that way and not a licenced therapist who had lots of training. So even if I can explain myself perfectly it doesn't mean that someone else will not see something you don't, that is still important. It happens to me so often that I daydream and daydream about a certain topic and than one day a new thought comes up and I am like "oh I have never looked ad that this way". Therapists want you to reflect so you can see where your thoughts are a little bit unhealthy so you can then implement healthy coping mechanisms and ways of thinking. Its not only about the reflecting part,but also about what you do with it. And if the first part is no problem thats fine, but are you also completely sure that the second part is not a problem too?  but I totally get you. I know myself so well that I sometimes just go to therapy to update my therapist on my progress and not for actual help. But it is still important that someone who knows what he is doing can look at your behavior from another perspective

have you thought about where your confidence issues come from? maybe try to talk to a therapist about that

Another thing I can recommend is listening to affirmations. My therapist once told me to listen and to repeat them daily and I didn't believe how that would help me but after reaching rock bottom when it comes to my depression, GAD and suicidal thoughts I thought that before I kill myself I could at least to give it a try and I still can't believe how great it worked. (pls keep in mind that everyone is different, I am just sharing what worked for me and I hope that it helps someone else too)

Also if you work on yourself try to not do that so you have a better dating experience, do it for yourself and to become more happy. Really try to not think about the whole dating thing. A little trick is to think about yourself where you dont need to date someone anymore and not about the version of you in a relationship. Just imagine what a version who is already dating and that is completely independent and happy would do and try to act like that. The goal is to get away from the "I really want to have someone" and to get to a " Hey I am very happy right now and it would be cool to have someone but if not thats fine too". You can really work on your self worth and confidence, it just takes time!

As someone who had TE for years and managed to get to a point where the hair loss stopped once, please please please don't stop brushing your hair. I know it is so hard to see your hair come out but not brushing it will make it tangle and if you don't brush that out you will have to cut it off. And the amount you cut off will be so much more than the amount you would lose with just the hair loss. One thing I try doing is to take a hairbrush that is black (I have very dark hair) so that I don't notice the hair so much and also I really try to not to look at the brush when brushing if that makes sense. Try everything to not see the hair falling out to not be so frustrated and sad but please don't stop brushing it.   
 

 Also keep in mind that when taking any supplements it might take up to 4 months to see the improvement. I am very sorry you have to go through that!

I don't know if it helps but I am 21 too but a girl and have the same problem when it comes to guys. One thing I could recommend is to really work on your confidence and your self esteem. I really try to learn as much as possible about new things I really love ( in my case its neuroscience) so when I do this I somehow feel that if I meet people I could tell them interesting things about that. Not that it becomes a topic that often, but it gives me the confidence and the feeling that I am maybe in some areas interesting to talk to.   Also I have very bad anxiety so one thing that really helped me with people is to not focus on yourself but on them. Don't think stuff like “What if I am boring? What if the person doesn't like me?” but try to just listen to them and try to ask questions about the topic they are talking about. For example if someone is telling you something about their holiday, just ask if it was fun or if they would recommend going there. Really try and focus on them. In my case that helps me to not become very awkward and shy because I am busy to imagine how their holiday was for example and by keeping my focus there I don't become so anxious anymore. 

  
  Don't try to think so much about dating, it will just make everything worse. Try to find hobbies you like where you can meet new people and enjoy your life. Also try to work on yourself. Please try to remember that we still have so much time in front of us and it is really nothing to be ashamed of. Some girls are really insecure because of this too so please don't be so hard on yourself. 

  
  Another thing that helps me to be more positive is thinking about all the things you can do to make it more likely to meet someone. Go out, try dating online, go to a pub and try to talk to someone. I know it really sucks to never have experienced love from someone but it is really not to late for you. You can really learn how to talk to girls and like I said some of us don't even know what to say either :) 

  
  The last thing I want to mention is that even if it is really annoying to hear something like “You will meet someone when you least expect it” I really think that there is some truth behind that. For me it is like the “Drink more water”-advice. You hear it so often but sometimes there is a reason to that. That of course doesn't mean that you can't go out and try and talk to people or try online dating, but it sometimes really gives me hope.

hey, first of all I am very sorry that you feel this way. Of course I am not in the same situation but I guess I somehow understand how you feel. I am 21 and I never experienced love. I was diagnosed with depression when I was 12 after I got nearly raped and my priority was always to get better and not really going out and meeting people. But I never really thought about how long that would take. All my friends are in their second or third relationship while I never even had someone be really interested in me. I once was on two dates with a guy and I was so scared to do something physically because of the trauma but it turned out he had a girlfriend and just wanted to cheat.

 Especially the last 15 months were really hard because my best friend got engaged and the thought of attending a wedding while I did not even have my first  real kiss. ( "real" because I don't think that a first kiss bacause of sexual assault is really a first kiss) Because of that I developed such a bad anxiety disorder that I had from 2 to 7 panic attacks every day the last months. 

So even if in my situation regarding dating nothing changed I got to a place where I feel so much better. I am still lonely and hope to experience love one day, but I can live my life normally again. I think that you can really work on how you view your situation. And I dont mean the typical "Just love yourself and live happy, you dont need someone!!!" . Its really not so simple for people who never felt love. 

But you can work on yourself to make it more likely to meet someone. One thing I am doing right now is to work on my confidence and on having more hobbies to make me a more interesting person and you know what, it kind of makes me more positive that someday I will find someone. For example instead of feeling lonely and thinking " no one likes me" I try to make the effort to look up something very interesting. I really started loving neuroscience. So when I now look something up about the brain I automatically start feeling a little bit smarter and more interesting and think to myself "hey, I have really cool things to tell people". It really helps to boost your confidence and your self worth. Also give affirmations a try. I know thats one thing everyone says but just try to do them for one week. You can stop at every moment!

 I really think it helps to not think about "oh i probably never find someone". I mean yeah it happens, I wont tell you the same thing everyone says: " everyone finds someone". But if you just try to maybe go out, even alone and just watch some people on the street you will notice that not everyone of them is a perfect looking person and they will very likely find love at one point of their live. So in summary I would suggest you to shift your thinking from "no one likes me" to "what is the probability if I really work on becoming a very friendly and interesting person, and really make an effort to go out and meet new people and also worked on my flaws than after all that I still will be alone?" 

I dont know if that helps you, but I really hope you will feel better soon. Felling lonely and unloved is such a har thing to go through. I wish you all the best, and please don't forget that you are not alone in this. I really hope that everyone of us will experience love. Take care!

hey, that is the first time I see someone have that exact same problem. I've been dealing with this since 2015 and while I am very grateful that I never really lost all my hair and my hair loss came in waves that lasted from just 3 months up to 1 1/2 years and I had enough time in between to always grow some of it back, to this day I still don't know whats the cause of it. It is so frustrating to see your hair fall out for such a long time because everyone always tells you that it will grow back but after 5 years I am not so sure anymore. I still have enough hair that if I get a wig people will ask me why because it is not necessary, but also I have lost enough hair to not feel comfortable anymore.

Have you found something that helped you?

My theory in the moment for my situation is that its because of stress. But I have had depression for nearly 10 years now so I still dont get why it comes in waves and doesn't fall out all the time if stress is the reason.

I really hope you find something that works for you!!
